title: Comparative Veterinary Anatomy & Physiology For The Veterinary Technician
description: Comparative veterinary anatomy and physiology for veterinary technicians. Clinically relevant veterinary anatomy and physiology, including a discussion of the similarities and differences among the major domestic species. Emphasis is placed on the normal structure and function of the major organ systems as the foundation for understanding pathology and the pathophysiology of disease. Intended for students in the Veterinary Technology Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Know and explain the normal physiology of selected organs and organ systems of domestic animals and relate it to the clinical practice of veterinary technology.
Recognize and identify the normal anatomy of selected organs and organ systems of domestic animals and relate it to the clinical practice of veterinary technology.
objectives: Analyze and evaluate the relationship between cell structure and function, and the mechanisms in place to maintain homeostasis at the cellular level
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between integumentary system structure and function, and the role of the integumentary system in maintaining homeostasis in a variety of domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between skeletal system structure and function, and the role of the skeletal system in maintaining homeostasis in a variety of domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between muscular system structure and function, and the role of the muscular system in maintaining homeostasis in a variety of domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between cardiovascular system structure and function, and the role of the cardiovascular system in maintaining homeostasis in a variety of domestic species
Analyze and evaluate the relationship between respiratory system structure and function, and the role of the respiratory system in maintaining homeostasis in a variety of domestic species
content: Introductory unit on anatomy and physiology will include:
General plan of the animal body
The integumentary system in a variety of animal species
Application of integumentary system in clinical practice
Application of skeletal system in clinical practice
Application of cardiovascular system in clinical practice
Application of respiratory system in clinical practice
lab: Cell and tissue identification using prepared slides
Integument: identification and description of function
Skeletal: identification of bones and joints
Muscular: identification of muscles, describe function
Cardiovascular: dissection of heart, explain function
Respiratory: dissection and description of respiratory system
Participate in a necropsy procedure to better understand systems taught this quarter
